item.title: Trump Officials Draft Plan to Pay At-Home Parents, Using Funds for Working Ones
item.author: Coral Davenport
item.content:encoded: The proposed benefit, a top policy priority for Vice President JD Vance, would apply only to married couples and tap a fund intended to provide federal child care subsidies to working parents.

item.title: Trump’s Super PAC to Pump $10 Million Into Texas to Boost Paxton
item.author: Bill Allison
item.content:encoded: President Donald Trump’s super political action committee is spending $10 million to back Republican Ken Paxton’s US Senate bid in Texas, its biggest expenditure yet in this election cycle, according to a filing with the Federal Election Commission.

item.title: Trump’s Super PAC Will Spend $10 Million on Texas Senate Race
item.author: Theodore Schleifer
item.content:encoded: A financial filing announcing the TV and digital ad buy is the first general election spending by MAGA Inc. The group intends to boost the Republican nominee, Ken Paxton.

item.title: Nigel Farage’s Reform Hits Roadblocks in Quest for UK Power After Funding Sting
item.author: Lucy White, Katherine Griffiths and Jacob Reid
item.content:encoded: Reform UK billed its 2026 conference as a showcase for policies it would implement during its first 100 days in power. In the end, the gathering served to highlight the mounting obstacles to Nigel Farage’s party winning office.

item.title: What the War in Iran Has Cost One Gold Star Family
item.author: Katie Rogers
item.content:encoded: First Lt. Tyler James Feehan, who was 25, had been deployed to an air base in Jordan when enemy missiles and drones lit up the sky. He is among the 18 Americans who have died since the war began.

item.title: Greek Premier Unveils €2.2 Billion in Economic Support for 2027
item.author: Sotiris Nikas
item.content:encoded: Greek Prime Minister Kyriakos Mitsotakis unveiled a package of economic measures worth €2.2 billion ($2.56 billion) in a bid to alleviate a cost of living crisis as the country gears up for national election next year.

item.title: Vannacci, Italy’s Rising Right-Wing Star, Has Yet to Meet Meloni
item.author: Donato Paolo Mancini and Chiara Albanese
item.content:encoded: Italy’s Roberto Vannacci, the insurgent ultranationalist, has yet to meet Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni or have contact with her circle, as his rise begins to reshape her right-wing alliance before next year’s election.

item.title: Is Work Starting for Trump’s Arch? It Depends Who’s Asking.
item.author: Emily Badger
item.content:encoded: The Justice Department told a court the government would only conduct archaeological excavation, a day after a Trump official announced the project was in motion.

item.title: Missouri Asks Supreme Court to Allow Voting Map Benefiting Republicans
item.author: Mitch Smith and Ann E. Marimow
item.content:encoded: Missouri’s Supreme Court said a map redrawn to help Republicans could not be used in November and said voters should decide on the new boundaries.

item.title: Ossoff and Talarico to Share Fund-Raising Event in Hollywood
item.author: Theodore Schleifer
item.content:encoded: The event with the Georgia and Texas Democrats will be hosted by Shonda Rhimes.

item.title: Portugal Sees No Threat to Schengen From Ceuta Migrant Surge
item.author: Donato Paolo Mancini and Tiago Ramos Alfaro
item.content:encoded: A surge of migrants into the Spanish exclave of Ceuta this summer didn’t pose a threat to the European Union’s free-travel zone, Portugal’s foreign minister said on Saturday.

item.title: Spotify’s Lorentzon Says He’d Leave Sweden If Wealth Tax Imposed
item.author: Rafaela Lindeberg
item.content:encoded: Spotify Technology SA co-founder Martin Lorentzon said he would leave Sweden immediately if the country introduces new wealth taxes, escalating concerns that proposals being debated ahead of this month’s election could drive entrepreneurs and capital abroad.

item.title: Trump’s Embrace of AI Data Centers Adds to GOP’s Midterm Peril
item.author: Courtney Subramanian, Jennifer A. Dlouhy and Steven T. Dennis
item.content:encoded: President Donald Trump’s fervent support for artificial intelligence data centers has put him at odds with voters who increasingly oppose them and comes despite direct warnings that his stance threatens to deepen Republicans’ peril in the November midterm elections.

item.title: US Strikes 3 Iranian Tankers in Retaliation for IRGC Attacks
item.author: Kevin Whitelaw
item.content:encoded: The US military said it launched strikes against three Iranian crude oil tankers in retaliation for the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps targeting two US Navy warships with ballistic missiles.

item.title: German Police Secure Explosive Devices Targeting Power Grid
item.author: Christina Kyriasoglou and Eva Brendel
item.content:encoded: Police in Germany discovered 12 explosive devices near overhead power lines in two districts in the country’s east, the latest in a spate of incidents targeting the country’s electricity infrastructure.

item.title: Trump Oil Deal Blindsides US Energy Companies
item.content:encoded: US oil executives say they were blindsided by the Trump administration’s Venezuela deal, which gives North American Blue Energy Partners access to fields that other companies had been pursuing. Bloomberg News White House Reporter Jennifer Dlouhy and Wall Street Journal National Security Reporter Vera Bergengruen are on Bloomberg This Weekend and say industry figures are also questioning whether the company can quickly develop new production and whether the arrangement can deliver lower gasoline prices before the midterm elections. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Missouri Asks US Supreme Court to Restore GOP-Backed Voting Map
item.author: Madlin Mekelburg
item.content:encoded: Missouri and its Republican leaders asked the US Supreme Court to reinstate a congressional map engineered by GOP lawmakers in the state to favor the party in November’s midterm elections.

item.title: Putin Orders No Airstrikes on Kyiv While US Envoys Visit
item.author: Ros Krasny
item.content:encoded: Russian President Vladimir Putin has ordered Kremlin troops not to fire on Kyiv for three days as US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner prepare to visit, Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov told Interfax.

item.title: US Envoys Due in Kyiv After Putin Says Ending War ‘Not Simple’
item.author: Bloomberg News
item.content:encoded: Russian President Vladimir Putin hosted US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner for more than three hours of talks in Moscow that a Kremlin aide called “highly useful,” setting the stage for the pair’s planned trip to Kyiv to meet Ukrainian leaders on Sunday.

item.title: Gallup Polls Show Democrats Outnumber Republicans Ahead of 2026 Midterm Elections
item.author: Ruth Igielnik and Caroline Soler
item.content:encoded: Data from Gallup shows that Democrats and Democratic-leaning independents have their largest advantage over Republicans since 2008.

item.title: Looking Back on the Summer of High MAGA in Trump's Washington
item.author: Shawn McCreesh and Alex Kent
item.content:encoded: Racecars, crypto, billionaires, troops, sequins and a bloody cage fight.

item.title: Kyiv Adapts to Constant Attack by Russian Jet-Powered Drones
item.author: Volodymyr Verbianyi and Olesia Safronova
item.content:encoded: As a resident of Boryspil, a satellite town of Kyiv, Kostyantyn Kuts has grown accustomed to regular night-time air raids. This past week has been different.

item.title: ‘We Can Only Win’: The Rise of the Far Right in Eastern Germany
item.author: Kamil Kowalcze
item.content:encoded: In a village on the edge of Germany’s Harz mountains, families gathering at a beer-and-bratwurst summer picnic lined up for autographs and selfies from the man they want to lead the country’s first far-right state government since World War II.

item.title: Burnham Gets His Own Breathing Space as Turmoil Engulfs Farage
item.author: Alex Wickham
item.content:encoded: Andy Burnham was just starting to face awkward questions about his plans as Britain’s prime minster this week. Instead, his biggest rival, Nigel Farage, ended up being the one under greater pressure to explain.

item.title: Former Kentucky Governor Is Arrested Amid Child Support Battle
item.author: Ishani Desai
item.content:encoded: Matthew Bevin, the former Republican governor, was held in contempt for failing to abide by court orders to file financial disclosure documents, a lawyer said.

item.title: In Major Leak Hunt, Pentagon Gives Polygraph Tests to Joint Staff Members
item.author: Jonathan Swan, Adam Entous, Maggie Haberman and Eric Schmitt
item.content:encoded: About 50 people were tested, an unparalleled inquiry that comes in the wake of news reports about the war with Iran and the U.S. military’s diminished stocks of munitions.

item.title: Tetris Distances Itself From White House’s Wall-Building Game
item.author: María Paula Mijares Torres
item.content:encoded: The maker of Tetris criticized a new White House digital game that mimics its classic puzzle by having players build a wall to stop migrants from crossing the US border.

item.title: Judge Will Not Block Pentagon Move to Fire Stars and Stripes Journalists
item.author: Chris Cameron and Erik Wemple
item.content:encoded: A judge appeared skeptical of the journalists’ arguments that they were fired for coverage of worsening conditions on a Navy warship.

item.title: Judge Once Again Blocks Trump Administration’s Plans to Restrict Mail-In Ballots
item.author: Zach Montague
item.content:encoded: The ruling arrived before the Supreme Court could decide whether to intervene but appeared certain to set off yet another round of appeals.

item.title: Trump Says He Will Spend Some of His War Chest on Republicans
item.author: Luke Broadwater
item.content:encoded: President Trump said he intends to hold some money back, even as Republican candidates ask for financial support.

item.title: Postal Service Internal Watchdog Opens Inquiry After Whistle-Blower’s Complaint
item.author: Eileen Sullivan
item.content:encoded: The Trump administration’s effort to screen mail-in ballots for the midterms is facing numerous challenges.

item.title: North Carolina Adds New Restrictions to Vote-by-Mail Program
item.author: Emily Davies
item.content:encoded: The changes are almost certain to cause some votes to be tossed. They come at a time when President Trump is promoting false claims of widespread fraud in mail voting.

item.title: Trump’s Latest Clemency Grants Benefit Drug Offenders, Union Boss
item.author: Kenneth P. Vogel
item.content:encoded: The president issued pardons or commutations to 30 people on Thursday, continuing his unorthodox and unpredictable use of clemency power.

item.title: The Tetris Company Denounces Trump White House Clone of Tetris
item.author: Chris Cameron
item.content:encoded: Responding to Build the Wall, an apparent copy of the retro video game, the Tetris Company said “we take copyright infringement very seriously.”

item.title: C.D.C. Says No Deaths This Year Attributed to Measles
item.author: Apoorva Mandavilli
item.content:encoded: The agency’s weekly update escalates a political fight after Pennsylvania said two deaths had been caused by the virus.

item.title: Ambassador Who Removed Kehinde Wiley Work Described It as a Lesbian Picnic
item.author: Zachary Small
item.content:encoded: Trump officials recently removed a painting from the U.S. Embassy in the Dominican Republic without explaining why. An interview by Ambassador Leah Campos shed some light.

item.title: What to Know About Trump’s Efforts to Block Mail-in Ballots
item.author: Reid J. Epstein
item.content:encoded: We sort through the proposed changes and court challenges, less than two months from Election Day.

item.title: Xi’s Personnel Reshuffle Picks Up Pace as New Faces Emerge
item.author: Bloomberg News
item.content:encoded: China has named a former vice finance minister as acting mayor of Shanghai, the latest in a string of appointments ahead of a key congress for the ruling Communist Party next year.

item.title: Greek Premier Plans Fresh Economic Support as Election Nears
item.author: Sotiris Nikas
item.content:encoded: Greek Prime Minister Kyriakos Mitsotakis is about to unveil an economic support package aimed at alleviating a cost of living crisis as he lays out his broader economic agenda ahead of next year’s national elections.
